title: Three sentenced to nearly 40 years in Laredo-linked firearms trafficking case
excerpt: Three people were sentenced in federal court in Del Rio to a combined 39 1/2 years in prison after pleading guilty in a firearms trafficking conspiracy that moved guns from the United States into Mexico through Laredo.
content:
Three people were sentenced in federal court in Del Rio this week to a combined 39 1/2 years in prison in a firearms trafficking case tied to Laredo, according to the Laredo Morning Times, citing the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Texas.

Edgar Josue Montelongo-Loera, 39, was sentenced to 15 years; Reymundo Hernandez-Nino, 41, to 12 1/2 years; and Kenia Lizbeth Montelongo, 31, to 12 years. All three pleaded guilty earlier in 2026 to charges related to trafficking firearms from the United States to Mexico.

According to the original indictment, the three conspired to obtain and transport firearms without the authorization required to export firearms and ammunition to Mexico, and aided the purchase, transportation, concealment, storage and sale of the firearms before their export or attempted export, the Laredo Morning Times reported.

The conspiracy ran from May 2024 through July 2025, according to the indictment. Between May and July 2024, Montelongo bought seven .380-caliber pistols and a .22-caliber pistol, and in the days after each purchase she crossed into Mexico through Laredo, the newspaper reported. Montelongo-Loera was recorded crossing into Mexico in the same vehicle and displayed multiple firearms in social media profile pictures, according to the report.

In August 2024, agents with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives began reviewing WhatsApp conversations in which Montelongo-Loera discussed obtaining requested firearms and arranging transport, with additional conversations in November 2024, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

In July 2025, Montelongo-Loera was arrested after a co-conspirator was found attempting to smuggle eight handguns and 19 magazines into Mexico through the Eagle Pass Port of Entry. That co-conspirator told investigators he was paid $150 to $200 per firearm and had made 10 to 12 previous smuggling trips, the newspaper reported.

Two days after that arrest, federal agents searched Hernandez-Nino's residence in San Antonio, where Hernandez-Nino and Montelongo were arrested. Agents recovered 24 firearms there, including handguns, AR-15-style rifles and a shotgun, plus more than 4,000 rounds of ammunition and multiple sets of body armor, according to the report. Investigators determined the weapons, ammunition and accessories were bound for a Mexican drug cartel, which the article does not name.

The indictment identified 32 firearms by make, model and serial number, including Glock and Ruger pistols, AR-style rifles, a Remington rifle and a shotgun. Ten defendants were charged in the broader investigation; eight pleaded guilty and two remain scheduled for trial. Some documents, including the plea agreements, remain under seal, so the specific reasons for the sentence lengths are not publicly detailed, the Laredo Morning Times reported.

Source: Laredo Morning Times, Nov. 12, 2026.
